text: From the moment that you are dressed and go out, pocket all your knowledge with your watch, and never pull it out in company unless desired: the producing of the one unasked, implies that you are weary of the company; and the producing of the other unrequired, will make the company weary of you.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXX, to his son, London, November 1, Old Style 1750
